import re

def solve(env, goal):
    # Parse goal: "find two creditcard and put them in coffeetable."
    m = re.search(r'find (?:a |an |two |three )?(.+?) and put them in (?:a |an |the )?(\w+[\w ]*?)\.?$', goal, re.I)
    if m:
        obj_name = m.group(1).strip().lower()
        target_name = m.group(2).strip().lower()
    else:
        # fallback
        words = goal.lower().split()
        obj_name = "creditcard"
        target_name = words[-1].rstrip('.')

    # Determine required count
    count_words = {"a": 1, "an": 1, "one": 1, "two": 2, "three": 3, "four": 4,
                   "five": 5, "six": 6, "seven": 7, "eight": 8, "nine": 9, "ten": 10}
    required = 1
    gm = re.match(r'find (\w+)', goal.strip(), re.I)
    if gm and gm.group(1).lower() in count_words:
        required = count_words[gm.group(1).lower()]
    else:
        # check for number words anywhere before the object
        low = goal.lower()
        for w, c in count_words.items():
            if re.search(r'\b' + w + r'\b', low) and w not in ("a", "an", "one"):
                if low.index(w) < low.find(obj_name):
                    required = c
                    break

    def norm(s):
        return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s.strip().lower())

    obj_key = obj_name
    target_key = target_name

    # Track state
    inventory = []          # list of (obj_full, obj_base)
    seen_locations = {}     # loc name -> True (visited)
    containers = {}         # loc -> open/closed/None (for recep that need opening)
    known_items = {}        # loc -> set of item base names currently there
    current_loc = None
    moved_count = 0
    place_candidates = []   # receptacles we might place into

    # Parse room description for receptacles
    def parse_receptacles(text):
        # find the "you see ..." list
        lm = re.search(r'(?:you see|you can see|you notice)\s+(.+?)(?:\.|\n|$)', text, re.I)
        if not lm:
            # fallback: split by commas on whole text
            chunk = text
        else:
            chunk = lm.group(1)
        parts = re.split(r',\s*|\s+and\s+', chunk)
        out = []
        for p in parts:
            p = p.strip().rstrip('.')
            if not p:
                continue
            # remove leading a/an/the
            p2 = re.sub(r'^(a|an|the)\s+', '', p, flags=re.I).strip()
            if not p2:
                continue
            # ignore "nothing"
            if norm(p2) == "nothing":
                continue
            out.append(norm(p2))
        return out

    def parse_items(text):
        # Look for "you see a X, a Y, ..." or "In it, you see ..." or "On the X, you see ..."
        lm = re.search(r'(?:you see|you can see|you notice)\s+(.+?)(?:\.|\n|$)', text, re.I)
        if not lm:
            return []
        chunk = lm.group(1)
        parts = re.split(r',\s*|\s+and\s+', chunk)
        items = []
        for p in parts:
            p = p.strip().rstrip('.')
            if not p:
                continue
            p2 = re.sub(r'^(a|an|the)\s+', '', p, flags=re.I).strip()
            if not p2:
                continue
            if norm(p2) == "nothing":
                continue
            items.append(norm(p2))
        return items

    def base_of(name):
        # strip trailing number id: "creditcard 2" -> "creditcard"
        return re.sub(r'\s+\d+$', '', name).strip()

    def is_obj(item, key):
        b = base_of(item)
        return b == key or b.startswith(key) or key in b

    def is_target(name, key):
        return norm(name) == key

    # Initial room parse
    obs = env.observation
    receptacles = parse_receptacles(obs)
    # current room has no "current_loc" yet

    # We'll do a systematic exploration:
    # 1) Go to every receptacle, look/open if needed, collect items.
    # 2) Once we have required items in inventory, go to target and drop.

    def go(loc):
        nonlocal current_loc
        if current_loc == loc:
            return
        r = env.step("go to " + loc)
        current_loc = loc
        return r

    def look():
        return env.step("look")

    def open_loc(loc):
        return env.step("open " + loc)

    def close_loc(loc):
        return env.step("close " + loc)

    def take(item, loc):
        return env.step("take %s from %s" % (item, loc))

    def drop(item, loc):
        return env.step("move %s to %s" % (item, loc))

    def inventory_list():
        nonlocal inventory
        r = env.step("inventory")
        m2 = re.search(r'you are carrying:?\s*(.*?)(?:\.|\n|$)', r, re.I)
        if m2:
            chunk = m2.group(1).strip()
            if norm(chunk) == "nothing" or not chunk:
                inventory = []
            else:
            inventory = parse_items(chunk)
        return inventory

    # Explore. We want to be efficient (<=50 commands).
    # Strategy: visit receptacles, inspect contents (look/open), take matching items.
    # Keep track of visited to avoid re-visiting too much, but sometimes need to re-visit target.

    def inspect(loc):
        # returns list of visible items, opening if closed
        nonlocal containers
        if loc not in containers:
            containers[loc] = None
        # go
        go(loc)
        # if we know it's closed or unknown, try look first
        r = look()
        items = parse_items(r)
        # detect closed
        if re.search(r'\bclosed\b', r, re.I):
            r2 = open_loc(loc)
            containers[loc] = True
            items = parse_items(r2)
            # also check "In it, you see ..."
            if not items:
                items = parse_items(r2)
        return items

    # Better: parse from any text for items on/in
    def extract_items_from(text):
        res = []
        # "On the X, you see a, b"
        for m3 in re.finditer(r'(?:On|In|on|in) the [^,]+?, you see (.+?)(?:\.|$)', text):
            res.extend(parse_items("you see " + m3.group(1)))
        # "you see a, b"
        res.extend(parse_items(text))
        # dedupe preserve order
        seen = set()
        out = []
        for x in res:
            if x not in seen:
                seen.add(x)
                out.append(x)
        return out

    # Main loop
    # We'll keep a queue of locations to explore: all receptacles (maybe prioritize likely ones? just all)
    # But we must be efficient. 50 commands total. With ~15 receptacles, visiting all could be ~15*3=45 plus takes. Risky.
    # Better: prioritize receptacles likely to contain obj? Hard to know. But the example shows dresser had them.
    # Heuristic: names like dresser, drawer, cabinet, sidetable, coffeetable, sofa, armchair, table, shelf, box, fridge, safe, chest.
    # We'll just do BFS-ish but limit.

    # Let's just iterate receptacles, inspect, take matching until required count, then go place.
    # But we also need to place each one as we find it? No, we can carry multiple.
    # In example, they placed one, then went back and got another — because maybe they only took one at a time? Actually they took creditcard 2, placed it, then went back for creditcard 1.
    # That's because "move X to Y" might require holding it. They could have carried both. But example they did one at a time.
    # We can carry multiple: inventory check.
    # Simpler: as soon as we find an item, take it, go to target, drop it. Repeat until count reached.
    # This minimizes inventory complexity and follows example.

    # But going back and forth costs steps. Example did that and used ~38 steps. OK.
    # We'll do: inspect each receptacle; whenever we see matching item not yet placed, take, go target, drop.
    # But we need to avoid taking already placed ones (they're at target, not in receptacles).
    # We'll track moved_count.

    # Since we don't know where items are, we need to search. We'll search receptacle by receptacle.
    # Optimization: check target if it's a receptacle and might contain items? No, we're putting in target.
    # We'll skip target in search to save steps? But target could also contain items originally? Possibly. But we'll skip if already visited.
    # Actually we should search target too if we haven't found enough, but then we'd have to take from target — but goal is to put there, so if it already has them, done. So check target early: if it already has required count of obj, done.
    # We'll inspect target first.

    # Let's implement:
    placed_count = 0
    target_loc = None
    # Find target among receptacles
    for r in receptacles:
        if is_target(r, target_key):
            target_loc = r
            break
    if target_loc is None:
        # target not in initial list? Maybe it's an object we carry? Unlikely. Try just use target_key as loc.
        target_loc = target_key

    # Check target contents first
    # But we need to go there. We'll go and inspect.
    # However, if target is a container that's closed, open it.
    # We'll include target in search list but mark it specially.

    # Build search order: all receptacles except target first? Or target first to see if already has items.
    # Let's check target first.
    search_list = []
    if target_loc in receptacles:
        search_list.append(target_loc)
    for r in receptacles:
        if r != target_loc:
            search_list.append(r)
    if target_loc not in receptacles:
        # maybe target is not a receptacle in room; just add at end
        search_list.append(target_loc)

    # But we might also need to check containers inside containers? Not supported here.

    # We'll iterate search_list, inspect, take matching items, drop at target.
    # But we need to avoid infinite loops if item not found. We'll cap.

    # Track which items we've already taken/placed to avoid duplicates.
    taken_ids = set()

    # Also, we should refresh inventory to know what we carry (in case we take multiple).
    # We'll take one at a time and drop immediately.

    # We also need to handle "look" to see items in open container. We'll use env.step("look") after opening.

    # To save commands, we'll not "close" containers unless needed. Example closed them, but not necessary.
    # We'll just open and leave open.

    # Let's implement search:
    for loc in search_list:
        if placed_count >= required:
            break
        # Go to loc
        go(loc)
        # Look
        r = look()
        items = extract_items_from(r)
        # If closed, open
        if re.search(r'\bclosed\b', r, re.I):
            r2 = open_loc(loc)
            items = extract_items_from(r2)
            # Also check "In it, you see"
            items += extract_items_from(r2)
            # dedupe
            seen = set()
            tmp = []
            for x in items:
                if x not in seen:
                    seen.add(x)
                    tmp.append(x)
            items = tmp
        # Also if "In it, you see" but not closed
        # extract_items_from already handles "In it, you see"? Our regex requires "the X". "In it" won't match.
        # Let's add a manual search for "In it, you see"
        m4 = re.search(r'In it, you see (.+?)(?:\.|$)', r, re.I)
        if m4:
            items += parse_items("you see " + m4.group(1))
        # dedupe again
        seen = set()
        tmp = []
        for x in items:
            if x not in seen:
                seen.add(x)
                tmp.append(x)
        items = tmp

        # Check for matching objects
        for item in items:
            if placed_count >= required:
                break
            if is_obj(item, obj_key):
                # Take it
                take_r = take(item, loc)
                # Verify taken
                if "pick up" in take_r.lower() or "you pick up" in take_r.lower():
                    # Go to target
                    go(target_loc)
                    drop_r = drop(item, target_loc)
                    if "move" in drop_r.lower() or "you move" in drop_r.lower():
                        placed_count += 1
                # else maybe already taken? continue

        # After checking loc, if we have placed enough, break
        if placed_count >= required:
            break

    # If not enough placed, maybe we need to search more thoroughly (e.g., revisit with look).
    # But we cap at 50 commands. We'll just return.
    return
